author: Vox
description:
Voters in Washington, DC, and Denver, Colorado could soon ban one of the world’s most controversial foods: foie gras. 

French for “fatty liver,” many chefs and fine diners revere foie gras as a delicacy. But animal activists allege it’s particularly cruel, as it’s made by force-feeding ducks with a metal tube during the final weeks of their lives. If these two US cities do phase out foie gras sales, they’d join California, Brazil, and a number of US cities, including Pittsburgh, Portland, Oregon, and New York City.

author: Vox
description:
With the 2028 presidential election inching closer and closer, Democrats are turning their attention to universal child care as a key issue. They might not all agree yet on what “universal child care” means, but the fact that candidates are now rallying behind making early childhood more affordable and accessible is a testament to how successful the child care advocacy movement has been over the last decade.

author: Vox
description:
Why does sweating cool you down? When sweat evaporates, it carries heat away with it. Your fridge works the same way. A refrigerant inside turns from liquid to gas, pulling the warmth out of your food and releasing it into your kitchen. 

So how does a fridge make the coldest temperature in the universe? Watch Unexplainable on Netflix or listen wherever you get your podcasts.
